title: Larger physical volume and bounds on the number of matter fields in noncompact gauge theories on a lattice
abstract: The work was motivated by the numerical result that in a pure SU(2) gauge theory the ratio R of the effective non-compact and compact lattice spacing is larger than 1 and increasing with decreasing gauge coupling, as well as the expectation that it should further increase extending the parameter space. This means that with a noncompact regularization, at given number of lattice sites and comparable scaling, one can obtain a larger physical volume, whose importance for the control of size effects has long been known. We confirm qualitatively results and expectation by a perturbative evaluation of the effective lattice spacing in an expansion in the Plank constant of non-compact pure SU(2) and Abelian gauge theories, but we find in addition that R reaches the maximum value of sqrt(2). Including matter fields we find that R increases ( still up to sqrt(2) ) or decreases depending on the difference between the number of scalar and spinor degrees of freedom, and there are bounds on such a difference.
summary: This work analyzes noncompact gauge theories on a lattice to study the effective lattice spacing ratio, R. Using perturbative methods, the authors find that R is bounded, reaching a maximum of sqrt(2) for pure gauge theories. The inclusion of matter fields modifies this ratio, leading to constraints on the allowed difference between scalar and spinor degrees of freedom.
main_problem: The paper investigates the effective lattice spacing ratio (R) in noncompact gauge theories, determining how this ratio behaves when considering the inclusion of matter fields and establishing bounds on the number of matter fields.
main_result: For pure SU(2) and Abelian theories, the ratio R is found to increase up to a maximum value of sqrt(2). Including matter fields causes R to either increase or decrease, depending on the difference between scalar and spinor degrees of freedom, subject to specific bounds.
method: The analysis employs perturbative evaluation of the effective lattice spacing using an expansion in the Planck constant, alongside functional methods to determine the effective potential.
model_or_system: The study focuses on noncompact gauge theories formulated on a lattice, specifically examining pure SU(2) and Abelian gauge theories, and extending the analysis to include scalar ($\phi$) and spinor ($\psi$) matter fields.
key_observables: The ratio R of effective non-compact to compact lattice spacing, and the effective potential V.
important_parameters:
Gauge coupling constant (g), Planck constant (hbar), number of scalar ($

main_assumptions: The analysis is perturbative and restricted to $N_c=2$ for SU(2), with limitations noted regarding comparison to the Veneziano limit or asymptotic safety.
paper_structure: The paper builds from analyzing the pure gauge theory in the continuum limit, deriving the effective potential, and then incorporating matter fields to derive bounds on the degrees of freedom and the behavior of the ratio R in different dimensions (4D vs 3D).
why_interesting: While focused on lattice gauge theory, the rigorous derivation of bounds on field content and the study of effective parameters in a lattice regularization scheme are fundamental theoretical tools applicable to many-body physics models.
